title: Ops bendable capacity sprint digest — week of 2029-11-21
content:
Purpose:
This is the weekly digest for the 'bendable capacity' sprint — an experiment to blend reserved (dedicated) capacity, opportunistic fill, and short-lived spillover pools to reduce cold-starts and improve tail latency during regional surges. Notes below combine standup summaries, incident observations, key metrics, decisions, and action items for next week.

High-level summary:
- Experiment window: 2029-11-14 -> 2029-11-28 (current week is the middle of the window).
- Goal: reduce p99 latency during 5–10 minute surge windows by 15% while keeping incremental cost < 8% of baseline.
- Primary signal: priming_ratio (fraction of requests served from warm KV/prefix cache) + regional preemption signal.

This week at-a-glance:
- Warm cache priming rate improved from 48% -> 61% in west-us when bendable-capacity was active.
- Average GPU utilization across active bendable pools: 73% (target 70–85%).
- Notable regression: south-america region saw a transient 1100ms p95 spike on 11/20 05:30 UTC triggered by high preemption churn on opportunistic nodes.
- Canary for policy v2 (deprioritize preemptible eviction lists if priming_ratio < 0.5) rolled back after the spike; rollback decision captured below.

Standup snippets (daily highlights):
- 11/19 — Marcus: started telemetry filter to tag requests used for priming metrics; found skew from internal test harness generating many short queries. Action: filter internal-tests in pipeline (INF-846).
- 11/20 — Sofia: observed preemption cascade in sa-east1; traced to spot autoscaler using aggressive scale-in window. Added cooldown (30m->90m) to opportunistic pools as experiment.
- 11/21 morning — Diego: ran synthetic surge replay for 12 minutes at 3x baseline; bendable pools reduced p99 by 18% in eu-west while adding +5% cost. Noted more frequent KV hot-set eviction; follow-up to tune cache admission.

Incident recap (11/20 sa-east1 spike):
- Time: 2029-11-20 05:30 UTC
- Symptom: p95 increased from 420ms -> 1530ms for ~7 minutes; increased 502 errors from dependent routing (fallbacks tripped).
- Root cause: opportunistic node preemptions overlapped with an autoscaler misestimate; many in-region replacements came online cold and attempted to route cached prefixes while cache warmers were throttled.
- Mitigations applied: reverted policy v2 and temporarily increased dedicated burst capacity for sa-east1 by +3 GPUs; enabled cross-region spillover to eu-west.
- Postmortem status: P1, initial notes drafted (INF-850). Full blameless writeup scheduled 11/23.

Metrics (week aggregated):
- priming_ratio (global): baseline week 51% -> experiment week 59%
- p50/p95/p99 token-gen latency (global): 110ms / 410ms / 980ms -> 105ms / 360ms / 825ms
- GPU idle seconds reclaimed by opportunistic fill: 1.8M sec -> reclaimed 2.4M sec
- Cost delta (mid-week estimate): +4.6% vs baseline (within target)

Decisions made:
1) Rollback policy v2 in sa-east1 after the 11/20 incident. Rationale: policy reduced preemption sensitivity and caused local fragility under heavy scale-ins. Action: iterate offline on a hybrid policy that considers priming_ratio, recent preemption rate, and queue depth. Owner: Sofia. Target: prototype by 11/27.
2) Keep bendable capacity enabled in eu-west, west-us and ap-south for remainder of experiment (early telemetry favorable). Owner: Diego.
3) Increase opportunistic pool scale-in cooldown to 90m for all SA regions for next 2 weeks. Owner: Marcus.
4) Add additional warm-cache metrics: eviction_rate_by_prefix, priming_latency_p90. Owner: Priya.

Action items (with owners and rough ETA):
- INF-846: Exclude internal test traffic from priming metrics (Marcus) — ETA 2029-11-23
- INF-850: Full incident postmortem (Sofia + Diego) — ETA 2029-11-23
- INF-859: Tune cache admission thresholds to reduce hot-set eviction (Diego) — ETA 2029-11-29
- INF-862: Prototype hybrid preemption policy that factors priming_ratio and recent preemption rate (Sofia) — ETA 2029-11-27
- INF-865: Dashboard tiles for eviction_rate_by_prefix and priming_latency_p90 (Priya) — ETA 2029-11-24
- Infra on-call: prepare surge-playbook runbook for blackouts longer than 10m (rotation owners: Marcus -> Priya) — ETA 2029-11-26

Open questions & hypotheses to validate:
- How much of the priming_ratio improvement is from better routing vs. actual KV cache warming? We need request traces with KV-hit tags to disambiguate.
- Hypothesis: Slightly longer token-level batch windows during priming windows reduces KV eviction without hurting p50. Experiment: +5ms batch window during first 30s of a user session.
- Evaluate cost effectiveness for customers on Dedicated vs Hosted tiers; initial split suggests Hosted usage benefits most from bendable pools due to higher cold-start sensitivity.

Notes on runbooks and playbooks:
- We introduced a short 'preemption cascade' checklist this week: checks for recent autoscaler changes, warm-cache-hit ratio, and opportunistic scale-in events in the preceding 15 minutes. It's in the playbook draft (confluence link above).
- Suggestion: add a single-button rollback in the console to revert regional bendable policies (owner: product-infra).

Next week priorities (top 5):
1) Complete INF-850 postmortem and action list.
2) Deploy eviction_rate_by_prefix metric and observe for 48h.
3) Prototype hybrid preemption policy and run small 10% canary in sa-east1.
4) Run a controlled synthetic 20-minute surge on 11/26 to validate p99 improvements at scale.
5) Finalize cost analysis and document customer impact for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Appendix: quick commands & references
- Repro script for synthetic surge: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/playbooks/surge-replay.sh
- Scheduler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-scheduler/pull/512 (contains policy v2 and rollback code)
- Linear board: https://linear.app/RW/board/infrastructure-capacity/sprint/22

Notes to reviewers:
- Please sanity-check the cost deltas against billing-export (I attached a sample CSV to the infra-team slack channel).
- If you are on-call next week and get a regional latency spike, follow the new checklist and escalate to the capacity pager if rollback is necessary.

End of digest.
(Quick editorial note: this doc is intentionally conversational — it's the working digest for the bendable capacity experiment. For the formal postmortem and final experiment report we will migrate clean copies to Confluence.)
